cards.title: Verbs
rule: Definition: Verbs & Auxiliary Verbs (ግሶችን ሓገዝቲ ግሶችን) refers to the syntactic system that combines lexical main verbs (which convey action, occurrence, or state of being) with primary auxiliary verbs (*be, do, have*) to express grammatical tense, aspect, mood, voice, and negation.

English verbs are fundamentally divided into lexical/main verbs (ቀንዲ ግሶች) and auxiliary/helping verbs (ሓገዝቲ ግሶች). Main verbs carry the core semantic meaning of the sentence, while auxiliary verbs are functional elements that modify the main verb to specify grammatical parameters. Lexical verbs are morphologically categorized as either regular or irregular based on how they form their past simple ($$\text{V}_2$$) and past participle ($$\text{V}_3$$) states. Regular verbs follow a predictable morphological rule of adding the suffix $$\text{Verb} + \text{-ed}$$ (e.g., *work/worked/worked*). Irregular verbs, however, do not follow this rule and undergo internal vowel mutations (e.g., *sing/sang/sung*), consonant shifts (e.g., *bend/bent/bent*), or show zero morphological change (e.g., *put/put/put*). This irregular pattern is structurally foreign to Tigrinya speakers because Tigrinya uses a non-concatenative root-and-pattern Semitic morphology (ሱር-መሰረት ግሲ) where verbs are derived from consonantal roots through highly predictable vowel templates. Consequently, English irregular verb forms must be systematically memorized for matriculation exams.

The primary auxiliary verb be (*am, is, are, was, were, been, being*) serves dual syntactic functions: it can act as a main copula verb or as a helping verb. As an auxiliary, 'be' is used to construct the continuous/progressive aspect ($$\text{be} + \text{V-ing}$$) and the passive voice ($$\text{be} + \text{V}_3$$). Tigrinya speakers often omit the 'be' auxiliary in their writing and speech (e.g., writing "She working" instead of "She is working"). This is because progressive aspect in Tigrinya can be marked morphologically directly on the main verb without requiring a separate auxiliary verb. In exams, distractors will often omit the auxiliary 'be' or present incorrect passive structures that test this exact syntactic requirement.

examples.text: She goes to school every day.
She go to school every day.
examples.fix: She goes to school every day.

cards.title: Notes
body: Definition: Verbs & Auxiliary Verbs (ግሶችን ሓገዝቲ ግሶችን) refers to the syntactic system that combines lexical main verbs (which convey action, occurrence, or state of being) with primary auxiliary verbs (*be, do, have*) to express grammatical tense, aspect, mood, voice, and negation.

English verbs are fundamentally divided into lexical/main verbs (ቀንዲ ግሶች) and auxiliary/helping verbs (ሓገዝቲ ግሶች). Main verbs carry the core semantic meaning of the sentence, while auxiliary verbs are functional elements that modify the main verb to specify grammatical parameters. Lexical verbs are morphologically categorized as either regular or irregular based on how they form their past simple ($$\text{V}_2$$) and past participle ($$\text{V}_3$$) states. Regular verbs follow a predictable morphological rule of adding the suffix $$\text{Verb} + \text{-ed}$$ (e.g., *work/worked/worked*). Irregular verbs, however, do not follow this rule and undergo internal vowel mutations (e.g., *sing/sang/sung*), consonant shifts (e.g., *bend/bent/bent*), or show zero morphological change (e.g., *put/put/put*). This irregular pattern is structurally foreign to Tigrinya speakers because Tigrinya uses a non-concatenative root-and-pattern Semitic morphology (ሱር-መሰረት ግሲ) where verbs are derived from consonantal roots through highly predictable vowel templates. Consequently, English irregular verb forms must be systematically memorized for matriculation exams.

The primary auxiliary verb be (*am, is, are, was, were, been, being*) serves dual syntactic functions: it can act as a main copula verb or as a helping verb. As an auxiliary, 'be' is used to construct the continuous/progressive aspect ($$\text{be} + \text{V-ing}$$) and the passive voice ($$\text{be} + \text{V}_3$$). Tigrinya speakers often omit the 'be' auxiliary in their writing and speech (e.g., writing "She working" instead of "She is working"). This is because progressive aspect in Tigrinya can be marked morphologically directly on the main verb without requiring a separate auxiliary verb. In exams, distractors will often omit the auxiliary 'be' or present incorrect passive structures that test this exact syntactic requirement.

The primary auxiliary verb have (*have, has, had, having*) is used to form the perfect aspect ($$\text{have/has/had} + \text{V}_3$$), representing completed actions with current relevance. Present perfect relates past events to the present, whereas past perfect ($$\text{had} + \text{V}_3$$) sequences two past events, marking the earlier action. Tigrinya lacks a direct morphological equivalent to the English Present Perfect tense. It instead relies on a gerundive form (e.g., "መጺኡ" - *he has come/he came*) or the past tense suffix. This grammatical difference makes it difficult for Tigrinya speakers to distinguish between the simple past ($$\text{V}_2$$) and the present perfect ($$\text{have/has} + \text{V}_3$$), a distinction that is a core topic in high-stakes English exams.

cards.title: Use the correct verb form after modals and auxiliaries
cards.problem: Correct the verbs: "She can sings well, and she has wrote three songs, but she don't like performing."

steps.text: **Step 1: Modal + base form.** can sings → can **sing**.
**Step 2: have/has + past participle.** has wrote → has **written**.
**Step 3: Third-person singular negative uses doesn't + base.** she don't → she **doesn't** like.
**Tip:** after a modal or do/does/did, the main verb never takes -s, -ed or -ing.

cards.answer: She can sing well, and she has written three songs, but she doesn't like performing.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Since the local library was renovated last year, the number of visitors ________ significantly.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject is 'the number of visitors' (singular). The sentence describes an action that started in the past (renovated last year) and continues to have relevance in the present, requiring the present perfect tense ($$\text{has/have} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'visitors' (plural) and choose 'have increased' (Option B). However, 'The number of' is singular, requiring the singular auxiliary 'has'. Simple past 'increased' (Option C) is incorrect because the sentence links the past action to the present status.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'the number of' (ቁጽሪ ናይ...) ስለ ዝኾነ ነጸላ (singular) እዩ። ስለዚ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ሓገዝቲ ግሲ 'has' (Option A) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። 'visitors' (ኣጋይሽ) ዝብል ቃል ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ ስለ ዝኾነ ተማሃሮ 'have' ብምምራጽ ክጋገዩ ይኽእሉ እዮም።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The science teacher asked Dawit, 'Why ________ your assignment on time yesterday?'
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a direct question in the past simple tense. Questions require subject-auxiliary inversion: $$\text{Wh-word} + \text{auxiliary (didn't)} + \text{Subject (you)} + \text{base verb (complete)}$$.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option A incorrectly combines 'didn't' with the past tense verb 'completed'. Option B fails to invert the subject and auxiliary. In English, using 'did/didn't' requires the main verb to return to its base form, which is a highly tested rule on exams.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ሕቶ ክንሓትት ከለና እቲ ሓገዝቲ ግሲ ('didn't') ቅድሚ እቲ ዋና ባእታ ('you') ክስራዕ ኣለዎ። ከምኡ ውን 'did' ወይ 'didn't' ምስ ዝህልው፡ እቲ ቀንዲ ግሲ ወትሩ ናብቲ መበቆላዊ ቅጥዑ (base form - 'complete') ክምለስ ኣለዎ። ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option C እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check

options.A: The children have broke the window.
options.B: The children have broken the window.
options.C: The children has broken the window.
options.D: The children have breaked the window.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Present perfect: have/has + past participle.

**Step 2:** break – broke – broken; plural subject → have.

**Step 3:** Only the first option is correct.

**Tip:** Check three things in every verb: tense (time), voice (active/passive) and agreement (singular/plural). Irregular verbs must be memorised: go–went–gone.

questions.q: Since the local library was renovated last year, the number of visitors ________ significantly.
questions.label: 1. Since the local library was renovated last year, the number
why: The subject is 'the number of visitors' (singular). The sentence describes an action that started in the past (renovated last year) and continues to have relevance in the present, requiring the present perfect tense ($$\text{has/have} + \text{V}_3$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The science teacher asked Dawit, 'Why ________ your assignment on time yesterday?'
questions.label: 2. The science teacher asked Dawit, 'Why ________ your assignme
why: This is a direct question in the past simple tense. Questions require subject-auxiliary inversion: $$\text{Wh-word} + \text{auxiliary (didn't)} + \text{Subject (you)} + \text{base verb (complete)}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The rare African manuscript ________ from the national archives before the guards noticed the broken window.
questions.label: 3. The rare African manuscript ________ from the national archi
why: The sentence describes two past events: the manuscript being stolen and the guards noticing the broken window. The theft happened before the guards noticed it, requiring the past perfect passive voice ($$\text{had been} + \text{V}_3$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Each of the candidates who applied for the engineering position ________ a written test.
questions.label: 4. Each of the candidates who applied for the engineering posit
why: The subject of the sentence is 'Each' (singular), which always takes a singular verb and auxiliary ($$\text{Each} \rightarrow \text{singular verb}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Rarely ________ such an informative seminar on environmental preservation in our region.
questions.label: 5. Rarely ________ such an informative seminar on environmental
why: The sentence begins with the restrictive negative adverb 'Rarely'. This requires subject-auxiliary inversion ($$\text{Negative Adverb} + \text{Auxiliary} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The hens ________ three eggs in the nest yesterday, but a wild cat took them.
questions.label: 6. The hens ________ three eggs in the nest yesterday, but a wi
why: We need the past simple tense ($$\text{V}_2$$) of the transitive verb 'lay' (to place/produce eggs), which is 'laid' (lay/laid/laid).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The delegation from South Africa ________ arriving on the afternoon flight tomorrow.
questions.label: 7. The delegation from South Africa ________ arriving on the af
why: The subject is 'The delegation' (singular collective noun). The sentence describes a future progressive action, requiring the singular auxiliary 'is' ($$\text{is} + \text{V-ing}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: I don't think he ________ English fluently, although he has lived in London for two years.
questions.label: 8. I don't think he ________ English fluently, although he has
why: This is a simple present active statement with a singular subject 'he'. It requires the third-person singular verb 'speaks' ($$\text{Subject} + \text{Verb} + \text{-s}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Neither the school director nor the teachers ________ present at the emergency meeting yesterday.
questions.label: 9. Neither the school director nor the teachers ________ presen
why: When a compound subject is connected by 'neither... nor', the verb must agree with the closer subject. The closer subject is 'the teachers' (plural).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The political crisis in the neighboring country has ________ many citizens to flee their homes.
questions.label: 10. The political crisis in the neighboring country has ________
why: The auxiliary verb is 'has' (present perfect). It must be followed by the past participle ($$\text{V}_3$$) of the lexical verb, which is 'caused'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The lake ____ dry last summer because of the drought.
questions.label: 11. The lake ____ dry last summer because of the drought.
why: The past simple of the irregular verb "run" is "ran".
"has ran" mixes forms; the participle is "run".
questions.tip: Check three things in every verb: tense (time), voice (active/passive) and agreement (singular/plural). Irregular verbs must be memorised: go–went–gone.

questions.label: 12. Choose the correct past participle: "She has ____ three letters today."

questions.label: 13. Which verb is intransitive in this sentence? "The baby slept peacefully."

similar.q: Transitive or intransitive: "She opened the door."

why: An intransitive verb does not take an object.
"slept" has no object; "peacefully" is an adverb.

questions.q: Read: "The old well had been dug by the villagers in 1950. Over the years it dried up, so in 2015 a new pump was installed. Now the women do not walk for hours to fetch water." Which verb is in the past perfect passive?
questions.label: 17. Read: "The old well had been dug by the villagers in 1950. Over the years it dried up, so in 2015 a…

similar.q: Find the phrasal verb in the passage.

why: Past perfect passive = had been + past participle.
"dried up" is past simple active; "was installed" is past simple passive; "do not walk" is present simple.
